mainTopic: Which מעמד is cancelled on special days, הלל on ראש חודש as a custom, and the sources for the tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז
overview: The amud opens by asking why הלל cancels the מעמד of its own prayer time, while מוסף cancels the מעמד of נעילה. רב אשי shows that רבי יוסי holds מוסף cancels only its own מעמד, and the גמרא proves it by ruling out every other reading of his words. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה does not list ראש חודש ניסן. רבא answers that the הלל of ראש חודש is only a custom, which is backed by רבי יוחנן's list of full-הלל days, by a story about רב in בבל, and by a ברייתא. The גמרא then turns to the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז. Counting from מתן תורה through משה's forty days on the mountain shows that he broke the לוחות on the seventeenth of תמוז. The stopping of the תמיד and the burning of the תורה are known by tradition. רבא settles the clash between ירמיהו's ninth and the משנה's seventeenth by saying they describe two different destructions. A פסוק in דניאל dates the idol in the היכל, and רבא explains that there were really two idols, one of which broke. The report of what was found written there continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does הלל cancel its own watch but מוסף cancels a different one?
steps.stepSummary: A questioner points out that the משנה treats הלל and מוסף differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes הלל different, that it pushes aside its own מעמד, and what makes מוסף different, that it does not push aside its own מעמד?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone points out an inconsistency in the משנה. הלל cancels the מעמד of its own prayer time (שחרית), but מוסף seems to cancel the מעמד of a different time (נעילה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, each special feature of the day cancels one מעמד. For הלל, the cancelled מעמד is the one at the same time as הלל itself. For מוסף, the cancelled one is the מעמד of נעילה, which has nothing to do with מוסף. So the question is: why aren't they the same?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
A watch of ordinary Israelites who stood in for the nation during the קרבנות and gathered to pray
The additional offering (and its prayer) on special days

steps.confusionAlert: The word דידיה ('its own') refers to the מעמד that matches the same time slot. For הלל that is שחרית, and for מוסף that is the מעמד at the time of the מוסף prayer.

phrases.english: What is different about הלל, that it overrides its own [watch],
phrases.notes: 'Its own' means the מעמד of שחרית, the prayer when הלל is said.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מוּסָף דְּלָא דָּחֵי דִּידֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and what is different about the additional offering, that it does not override its own [watch]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by challenging how the משנה lists which מעמד is cancelled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מוסף cancels the מעמד of נעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל and מוסף should work the same way, yet one cancels its own time slot and the other cancels a different time slot.

steps.title: רב אשי: if מוסף cancels another watch, surely it cancels its own
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with a כל שכן: of course מוסף also cancels its own מעמד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Now, if it pushes aside a מעמד that is not its own, isn't it all the more so that it pushes aside its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tries to answer the question. He says מוסף does cancel its own מעמד too, and that follows from a כל שכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reasons that if מוסף is strong enough to cancel a distant מעמד (נעילה), it is certainly strong enough to cancel the מעמד at its own time. So in his reading, the משנה only mentions נעילה, and the מעמד of מוסף is cancelled without needing to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if (opens a 'how much more so' argument)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
Now, if it overrides [a watch] that is not its own,
phrases.notes: He means the מעמד of נעילה, which the משנה says מוסף cancels.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so [that it overrides] its own?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָאו דִּידֵיהּ דָּחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a כל שכן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: כל שכן: the stronger cancellation includes the weaker one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner seemed to assume מוסף does not cancel its own מעמד.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוסף cancels both its own מעמד and that of נעילה.

steps.title: The questioner clarifies: מוסף should cancel only its own watch
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains that his real point is the reverse: מוסף should cancel only its own מעמד, not נעילה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am telling you: it should push aside only its own!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner says רב אשי misunderstood him. He wasn't asking why מוסף doesn't cancel its own מעמד. He was asking why it cancels נעילה's מעמד at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the model of הלל, a feature of the day should cancel only the מעמד of its own time. So מוסף should cancel only the מעמד of מוסף and leave נעילה alone. This sharpens the challenge against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am saying to you (clarifying one's own question)

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
Let it override only its own [watch]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside רב אשי's answer by clarifying the original question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מוסף cancels the מעמד of נעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the pattern of הלל, מוסף should cancel only the מעמד of its own time, not a different one.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees with the questioner
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says every day with a מוסף has a מעמד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is רבי יוסי, who holds like you. As it is taught: רבי יוסי says: Every day that has a מוסף has a מעמד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי accepts the questioner's point and says a תנא already holds this way. He quotes רבי יוסי from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says that a day with מוסף still has a מעמד. He doesn't say which מעמד, so the גמרא will need to figure that out. That figuring out will prove the questioner's view.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ.
phrases.english: He said to him: There is Rabbi Yosei, who holds like you.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Any day that has an additional offering
has a watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the questioner's view from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The view that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד

steps.title: Which watch does רבי יוסי mean? Not שחרית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which מעמד רבי יוסי means and rules out the מעמד of שחרית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מעמד of which prayer? If you say the מעמד of שחרית, the תנא קמא also says that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a process of elimination to figure out which מעמד רבי יוסי is talking about. The first option, שחרית, is ruled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי meant the מעמד of שחרית, he would be saying nothing new, because the תנא קמא (the משנה) already agrees that a מוסף day keeps its שחרית מעמד. A תנא who is arguing must be saying something different, so this option fails.

phrases.english: The watch of which [prayer]?
If you say the watch of the morning prayer,

phrases.aramaic: הָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר!
phrases.english: but the first tanna also said so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts clarifying the vague term מעמד in רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which prayer's מעמד רבי יוסי says remains on a מוסף day
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not שחרית, since the תנא קמא already agrees about it

steps.title: Not the watch of מוסף either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out the מעמד of מוסף: could מוסף fail to cancel even its own?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the מעמד of מוסף? Does it not push aside even its own?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the מעמד of מוסף, and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that מוסף at least cancels the מעמד at its own time. It makes no sense to say that on a מוסף day the מעמד of מוסף still takes place. So רבי יוסי can't mean this.

phrases.english: Rather, the watch of the additional prayer —
does it not override even its own?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second option in the process of elimination, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי יוסי means the מעמד of מוסף
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is unthinkable that מוסף would not cancel even its own מעמד.

steps.title: Not the watch of מנחה, since even the wood offering cancels it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out the מעמד of מנחה, because the weaker קרבן עצים already cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the מעמד of מנחה? But the קרבן עצים pushes it aside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the third option, the מעמד of מנחה, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the קרבן עצים cancels the מעמד of מנחה. If the קרבן עצים, which is less important, cancels it, then מוסף, which is more important, certainly does. So רבי יוסי can't be saying that a מוסף day keeps its מנחה מעמד.

keyTerms.meaning: The wood offering brought by families on set days

phrases.english: Rather, [the watch] of the afternoon prayer —
but the wood offering overrides it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third option in the process of elimination, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי יוסי means the מעמד of מנחה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The weaker קרבן עצים already cancels the מנחה מעמד, so מוסף certainly would.

steps.title: It must be נעילה, so מוסף cancels only its own watch
steps.stepSummary: The only option left is נעילה, which proves that מוסף cancels its own מעמד but not another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it the מעמד of נעילה? Learn from this: it pushes aside its own, but it does not push aside what is not its own.
steps.whatsHappening: With every other option ruled out, the גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי means the מעמד of נעילה. That proves the questioner's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says a מוסף day still has a מעמד at נעילה. So according to him, מוסף does not cancel a מעמד that isn't its own. It cancels only the מעמד of its own time, just like הלל, and this is exactly what the questioner argued in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not... (introduces the only remaining option)
The closing prayer at the end of the day

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, מוסף cancels only its own מעמד, not the מעמד of נעילה. This matches the questioner's argument and differs from the תנא קמא of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not [the watch] of the closing prayer?
Learn from this: it overrides its own,
[but] what is not its own it does not override.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all other options are eliminated, draws the proof from רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaObject: The view that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ברייתא, read as referring to the מעמד of נעילה

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms the conclusion: indeed, learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא approves the proof. רבי יוסי really does hold that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing 'שמע מינה' shows that no one challenges the proof. The questioner's view now has a solid source in a תנא, רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference of step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי holds that מוסף cancels only the מעמד of its own time and not the מעמד of נעילה.

steps.title: Why not list the first of ניסן too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: ראש חודש ניסן seems to have all three features that cancel a מעמד, so it should be listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה should also teach: on the first of ניסן there was no מעמד, because it has הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה left out ראש חודש ניסן. That day seems to have הלל, a מוסף, and a wood offering, just like ראש חודש טבת, which the משנה did list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said ראש חודש טבת had no מעמד at all, because it had הלל, קרבן מוסף, and קרבן עצים. ראש חודש ניסן also has a מוסף, and it is one of the listed days for קרבן עצים. If it also has הלל, it should be on the list too.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it also teach. This asks why a case was left out.
Songs of praise said on special days
The wood offering brought by certain families on set days
The first day of a new month

phrases.english: And let it also teach:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
phrases.english: On the first of Nisan there was no non-priestly watch
because it has Hallel
and an additional offering and a wood offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling which מעמד is cancelled by מוסף, the גמרא checks whether the משנה's list of cases is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of days without a מעמד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש חודש ניסן seems to have all three features of ראש חודש טבת, so it should have been listed.

steps.title: הלל on ראש חודש is not a real obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה's silence shows that הלל on ראש חודש is not an obligation, so ראש חודש ניסן lacks the הלל feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this shows that the הלל of ראש חודש is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why ראש חודש ניסן is missing from the list. The הלל said on ראש חודש does not count, because it is not a real obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a required הלל pushes off the מעמד of שחרית. Since the הלל of ראש חודש is not required, ראש חודש ניסן does not have all three features. The ראש חודש טבת case worked only because it falls during חנוכה, which has a required הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: This is to say. It draws a conclusion from a source.
From the Torah, a real obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for treating הלל on ראש חודש as a custom rather than a requirement.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is to say
the Hallel of the New Moon
is not from the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means it isn't a required הלל at all, just a custom. The next steps show this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: one of the three features is not truly present.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראש חודש ניסן has a real הלל, so it should cancel the מעמד like ראש חודש טבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלל of ראש חודש is not an obligation, so ראש חודש ניסן is rightly left off the list.

steps.title: The list of days for full הלל leaves out ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's list of the 18 days (21 outside ארץ ישראל) for complete הלל does not include ראש חודש, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: on eighteen days a year an individual completes the הלל. They are the eight days of סוכות, the eight days of חנוכה, the first day of פסח, and the day of שבועות. In the Diaspora there are twenty-one: nine days of סוכות, eight of חנוכה, the first two days of פסח, and the two days of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא. It quotes a list of every day on which full הלל is said, and ראש חודש is not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside ארץ ישראל the count is 8+8+1+1=18. Outside it, the extra festival days make it 9+8+2+2=21. Since this is a complete list and ראש חודש is missing, the הלל of ראש חודש cannot be an obligation.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
Eighteen days a year
an individual completes the Hallel on them,
and these are they: the eight days of the Festival,
phrases.notes: "The חג" means סוכות, counted together with שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: and the eight days of Chanukah,
and the first festival day of Pesach,
and the festival day of Atzeret.
And in the Diaspora, twenty-one days,
and these are they: the nine days of the Festival,
and the eight days of Chanukah,
and the first two days of Pesach,
and the two festival days of Atzeret.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The הלל of ראש חודש is not an obligation
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's complete list of days for full הלל, which leaves out ראש חודש

steps.title: רב sees the Babylonians skipping parts of הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב saw people in בבל saying הלל on ראש חודש. He planned to stop them, but when he saw them skipping parts, he understood they were keeping a custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to בבל and saw them reading הלל on ראש חודש. He thought to stop them. Once he saw that they were skipping parts, he said: learn from this that they are keeping the custom of their forefathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that also shows הלל on ראש חודש is only a custom. רב first thought it was wrong, then saw they were treating it as a custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב worried that saying הלל on ראש חודש treated it like a required day. Their skipping of sections showed they knew it was not the full, required הלל. So he let them keep their custom.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come to a place

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to Babylonia,
he saw them reading Hallel
on the New Moon,
and he thought to stop them.
Once he saw
that they were skipping parts,
he said: Learn from this
the custom of their forefathers is in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that matches רבא's view that the הלל of ראש חודש is a custom.
steps.raayaObject: The הלל of ראש חודש is only a custom
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's reaction to the practice in בבל

steps.title: An individual should not start, but if he started he finishes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the practical rule: an individual should not begin the הלל of ראש חודש, but if he began, he finishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: an individual should not begin, but if he began, he completes it.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the practical rule for an individual about the הלל of ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because this הלל is only a custom, an individual praying alone is not told to start it. Still, once he has begun, he should not stop in the middle.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלל of ראש חודש is a custom, not a required הלל. That is why ראש חודש ניסן is not on the משנה's list.

phrases.english: It was taught:
An individual should not begin,
but if he began, he completes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical rule that follows from הלל on ראש חודש being a custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual should not start the הלל of ראש חודש, but if he started he should finish.

steps.title: How do we know the לוחות broke on the seventeenth of תמוז?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and asks for the source that the לוחות were broken on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things happened to our forefathers on the seventeenth of תמוז, etc. The לוחות were broken: how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, about the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז. It asks how we know the first one, the breaking of the לוחות, happened on that date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. The גמרא wants a source that pins the breaking of the לוחות to this exact date, and it will get there by counting days.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventeenth day of the month of תמוז
The stone tablets of the Ten Commandments

phrases.english: Five things happened to our forefathers
on the seventeenth of Tammuz, etc.
The tablets were broken: from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the לוחות were broken on שבעה עשר בתמוז

steps.title: The date the Ten Commandments were given
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute: the Ten Commandments were given on the sixth of the month, while רבי יוסי says the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: on the sixth of the month the Ten Commandments were given to ישראל. רבי יוסי says: on the seventh of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא about the date of מתן תורה. This sets the starting point for counting to the breaking of the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To find when the לוחות broke, the גמרא first needs to know when the counting starts. The ברייתא gives two opinions: the sixth or the seventh of סיון.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
On the sixth of the month
the Ten Commandments were given to Israel,
Rabbi Yosei says: on the seventh of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The starting date for the count: מתן תורה on the sixth (or, per רבי יוסי, the seventh) of סיון

steps.title: On the seventh, משה went up the mountain
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the Torah was given on the sixth, משה went up the mountain on the seventh. This begins the day count.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it was given on the sixth: it was given on the sixth, and on the seventh משה went up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out the timeline according to the first opinion. This is a setup line that prepares the count leading to the breaking of the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, the Torah was given on the sixth and משה went up on the seventh. The day משה went up is the starting point for the days that will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says, meaning according to that opinion

phrases.english: The one who says they were given on the sixth:
they were given on the sixth,
and on the seventh Moses went up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the date from step 16 to start the timeline.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first step of the timeline: מתן תורה on the sixth, and משה goes up on the seventh

steps.title: By both views משה went up on the seventh, so the forty days end on the sixteenth of תמוז
steps.stepSummary: By the view that the Torah was given on the seventh of סיון, משה went up that same day. His forty days on the mountain are counted as 24 days of סיון plus 16 days of תמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the Torah was given on the seventh: it was given on the seventh, and משה went up on the seventh. The פסוק says 'He called to משה on the seventh day,' and another פסוק says משה was on the mountain forty days and forty nights. The 24 days left in סיון plus 16 days of תמוז add up to forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that even by the view that the Torah was given on the seventh of סיון, משה still went up on the seventh. So both opinions agree on the starting day, and the forty-day count that follows works for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the giving of the Torah and משה going up both happened on the seventh, so both opinions agree that משה went up on the seventh. סיון has 30 days, so counting from the seventh through the thirtieth gives 24 days. Add 16 days of תמוז and you reach exactly forty, which sets up the next step: the next day is the seventeenth.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says. It introduces one side of a dispute.
They fill up to, they add up to.

phrases.english: The one who says: on the seventh
on the seventh they were given
phrases.notes: "They" are the עשרת הדברות, from the ברייתא in Step 16.

phrases.english: and on the seventh Moshe went up
as it is written: "And He called to Moshe on the seventh day"
and it is written: "And Moshe came into the midst of the cloud
and went up the mountain
and Moshe was on the mountain
forty days and forty nights"
twenty-four days of Sivan
phrases.notes: Count from the seventh through the thirtieth of סיון, including the day he went up. That gives 24 days.

phrases.english: and sixteen of Tammuz
add up to forty

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוסי's view also has משה going up on the seventh, matching Step 17, and then counts the forty days that apply to both views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה went up on the seventh of סיון, and his forty days ended on the sixteenth of תמוז.

steps.title: משה came down and broke the לוחות on the seventeenth of תמוז
steps.stepSummary: Right after the forty days, on the seventeenth of תמוז, משה came down, saw the עגל, and broke the לוחות. A פסוק confirms that he broke them when he reached the camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventeenth of תמוז he came down, came, and broke the לוחות. And it is written: 'When he came near the camp and saw the calf, he threw the לוחות from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it was asked for in Step 15. Since the forty days ended on the sixteenth, משה came down and broke the לוחות on the seventeenth of תמוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day count gave us the date, and the פסוק shows that the breaking happened as soon as משה came down to the camp. Together they answer the question of how we know the לוחות were broken on שבעה עשר בתמוז.

keyTerms.meaning: The tablets of the עשרת הדברות.

steps.whatToRemember: The day count from סיון through תמוז shows that משה came down on the seventeenth of תמוז and broke the לוחות that very day.

phrases.english: On the seventeenth of Tammuz he came down
came, and broke the tablets
And it is written: "And it was, when he came near the camp
that he saw the calf
and he threw the tablets from his hands
and broke them beneath the mountain"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the count from Step 18, which ended on the sixteenth, and lands on the seventeenth.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לוחות were broken on the seventeenth of תמוז, right after משה's forty days on the mountain.

steps.title: The daily offering stopping is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next tragedy listed in the משנה, the stopping of the תמיד, and says we know its date through a tradition passed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The תמיד stopped': this is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list. For the stopping of the תמיד, it does not bring a פסוק. It says the date is a tradition passed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the לוחות, the גמרא built a proof from פסוקים. Here it says the source is simply a tradition handed down, so no proof from a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering brought in the בית המקדש every morning and afternoon.
Here it means a tradition that was passed down.

steps.confusionAlert: In this step the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was received and passed down.

phrases.english: The daily offering stopped
It is a tradition

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the לוחות to the next tragedy in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date when the תמיד stopped is known through a tradition, not from a פסוק.

steps.title: Was the city really breached on the seventeenth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next tragedy, the breach of the city walls. It challenges the date with a פסוק in ירמיהו that seems to place the breach on the ninth of the fourth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The city was breached.' On the seventeenth? But it is written: 'In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine was severe in the city,' and right after it is written: 'And the city was breached.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה and attacks it. A פסוק seems to say the city was breached on the ninth of the month, not the seventeenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, the פסוק that says 'the city was breached' comes right after a date, the ninth of the fourth month. That makes it sound like the breach happened on the ninth. This is a direct clash with the משנה's date of the seventeenth. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? It brings a פסוק as a challenge.
The fourth month, counting from ניסן, which is תמוז.

phrases.english: The city was breached
On the seventeenth?
But isn't it written: "In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month
phrases.notes: The fourth month is תמוז, since we count from ניסן.

phrases.english: the famine was severe in the city"
and it is written right after it: "And the city was breached, etc."!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next tragedy in the משנה, but this time challenges its date instead of just finding a source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the city walls were breached on שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים in ירמיהו put the breach right after the date of the ninth of the fourth month, which suggests the breach happened on the ninth, not the seventeenth.

steps.title: First Temple on the ninth, Second Temple on the seventeenth
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the פסוק in ירמיהו describes the first בית המקדש, when the walls were breached on the ninth of תמוז. The משנה describes the second בית המקדש, when they were breached on the seventeenth. A ברייתא supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not a problem. Here (the פסוק) is about the first בית המקדש, and there (the משנה) is about the second. As a ברייתא teaches: At the first destruction the city was breached on the ninth of תמוז, and at the second, on the seventeenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from the last step. Both dates are correct because they are about two different destructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that ירמיהו gives the ninth of the fourth month, but the משנה says the seventeenth. רבא splits them: ירמיהו saw the first חורבן, and the משנה is talking about the second. The ברייתא states both dates outright, so his answer has support.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem. This opens an answer showing the two sources do not really clash.
At the first (destruction of the בית המקדש)
At the second (destruction of the בית המקדש)
The city was breached, meaning its walls were broken through

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה and ירמיהו argue about the date. Each is talking about a different חורבן, so both dates are true.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the fast is on the seventeenth of תמוז even though ירמיהו says the ninth. The fast follows the date of the second חורבן.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
Here, it is about the first [Temple],
phrases.notes: "Here" means the פסוק in ירמיהו from the last step.

phrases.english: there, it is about the second [Temple].
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
At the first, the city was breached on the ninth of Tammuz;
at the second, on the seventeenth of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא לא קשיא כאן בראשונה כאן בשניה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different destruction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like ירמיהו and the משנה disagree about the date of the breach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first חורבן was on the ninth of תמוז and the second on the seventeenth. The משנה follows the second.

steps.title: The burning of the תורה is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next tragedy, that אפוסטמוס burned the תורה, and says its date is known through a tradition passed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: אפוסטמוס burned the תורה: this is known by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list. It says we know the date of this event because it was handed down, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the stopping of the תמיד in step 20, there is no פסוק for this event. The source for the date is a tradition passed from teacher to student.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of an enemy who burned a ספר תורה
Here it means a tradition that was passed down

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was received and handed down.

phrases.english: Apostemos burned the Torah:
a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next tragedy in the משנה's list, using the same kind of answer as step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date is known by tradition.

steps.title: Where do we know the idol date from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next tragedy, that an idol was set up in the היכל, and asks how we know it happened on the seventeenth of תמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: An idol was set up in the היכל: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next tragedy and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether the idol was set up. It is how we know it happened on the seventeenth of תמוז.

keyTerms.meaning: The main building of the בית המקדש
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: He placed an idol in the Sanctuary:
from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He is asking how we know it was on the seventeenth of תמוז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next tragedy in the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for dating the idol in the היכל to the seventeenth of תמוז.

steps.title: The idol came when the daily offering stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in דניאל that links the stopping of the תמיד to the setting up of an abomination. Since the תמיד stopped on the seventeenth of תמוז, the idol was set up then too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And from the time the daily offering is removed, and the abomination that makes desolate is set up."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. The פסוק puts the idol at the same time as the stopping of the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 already set the date of the stopping of the תמיד as the seventeenth of תמוז. The פסוק ties the idol to that same moment, so the idol gets the same date.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering was taken away

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And from the time the daily offering is taken away
and the abomination that makes desolate is set up."

steps.triggerLanguage: דכתיב ומעת הוסר התמיד ולתת שקוץ שמם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דניאל links the idol to the day the תמיד stopped, which was the seventeenth of תמוז.

steps.title: Was there only one idol?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's mention of a single idol. Another פסוק in דניאל uses the plural, "abominations".
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there only one? But it is written: "And on the wing of abominations, the one that makes desolate"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה speaks of one idol, when another פסוק speaks of several.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the first פסוק say "an idol" and "abomination", in the singular. The פסוק in דניאל 9 says "abominations", in the plural, which means at least two. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? This brings a פסוק as a challenge.

phrases.english: And was there only one?
But isn't it written:
"And on the wing of abominations, the one that makes desolate"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וחד הוה והכתיב ועל כנף שקוצים משמם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea of a single idol from the last two steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a single idol was set up in the היכל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק uses the plural "abominations", which means more than one idol.

steps.title: There were two idols, but one broke
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there were two idols. One fell on the other and broke its hand, so only one stayed whole. He then begins to tell what was found written there, and this continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There were two. One fell on the other and broke its hand, and it was found that it was written:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the contradiction. The פסוק counts both idols, and the משנה counts only the one that stayed whole. He then starts to tell about writing that was found, and the quote continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were really two idols, which fits the plural "abominations". Because one fell and broke the other's hand, only one complete idol stood, which fits the משנה's singular. The final words open a new report about an inscription that is finished in the next part.
steps.whatToRemember: There were two idols but only one stayed whole. That is why the פסוק says "abominations" and the משנה speaks of one idol.

phrases.english: Rava said: There were two,
and one fell on the other
and broke its hand,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and it was found that it was written:

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא תרי הוו ונפל חד על חבריה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא about one idol versus many.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fitting both together: the פסוק counts both idols, and the משנה counts the one left whole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the פסוק's plural goes against the משנה's single idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two idols. One broke the other's hand, so only one complete idol remained.
